Subject: Inquiry: on-prem licensing + platform fee amortization

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking our call last week. We're moving forward with two pilot clusters for analytics workloads and need a clearer picture of Redwood's on-prem licensing model. Main questions from procurement and finance:

- How is the platform fee invoiced for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments? Monthly or annual? Can it be amortized across committed nodes?
- What volume / committed-capacity discounts do you offer for multi-cluster rollouts?
- Do you provide migration credits for customers who pay up-front for hardware but need assistance migrating tokens / data?

Can you share a pricing worksheet and sample T&Cs we can circulate internally? We're aiming to finalize pilot budgets by the end of July.

Best,
Aisha Patel
Procurement Manager
Strata Analytics

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a concise packet to start: Redwood_OnPrem_Pricing_v1.pdf (summary) and a linked worksheet we use to model committed discounts. High-level answers:

- Platform fee: invoiced monthly by default; annual prepay is possible with a 6% discount and can be amortized for internal accounting if you request an invoice schedule.
- Committed capacity discounts: tiered by reserved-GPU-equivalent and by length of commitment (12/24/36 months). We commonly structure an initial pilot at a reduced platform-fee rate, then step up on full rollout.
- Migration credits: offered as a one-time credit applied to platform fees (not hardware invoices). We typically grant 1-3 months of platform fee credit for pilots that convert to committed contracts; larger migration credit is negotiable for multi-region rollouts.

I'll set up a short call with Neha (pricing) and Marcus (SE) to align on the worksheet and any required SSO/KMS clauses in the SLA. Proposed times: Wed 7/15 10am ET or Thu 7/16 2pm ET.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Aisha — thanks for outlining procurement's constraints. Notes from our pricing side (see attached Pricing_Worksheet_Strata.xlsx for model):

- Amortization: we can provide an invoice schedule that aligns platform fees to a customer's internal accounting cadence. We cannot apply a credit directly to third-party hardware invoices, but we can issue a one-time credit against platform fees equal to the requested value. We will provide an accounting memo (signed) that details the credit application so your finance team can document it.

- Tier mapping (example, matched to common node sizes):
  * Pilot (1-10 nodes): platform fee = $5k/month (pilot rate)
  * Standard (11-50 nodes): 15% platform fee discount starting month 7 (after successful pilot conversion)
  * Enterprise (51+ nodes): 25% platform fee discount starting month 4; requires 12-month minimum commitment

- Migration credit phrasing for SOW (proposal):
  "Redwood will provide a one-time migration credit equal to three (3) months of the then-applicable platform fee, applied as a credit to the first invoice(s) following conversion from pilot to committed deployment. This credit is restricted to platform/service charges and does not apply to third-party hardware or network costs."

Happy to adjust numbers if you have a target budget. Marcus — can you confirm SRE/installation support assumptions and any additional scopes that might affect migration credit size?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick technical clarifications from the SE perspective:

- Installation support: our standard Private deployment package includes up to 3 days remote install + validation. On-prem physical installation or vendor-managed installs (on-site) are quoted separately. If Strata wants us to handle migration of KV caches or custom tokenizers, that is billable but we can include a limited scope (up to 40 engineer-hours) as part of the migration credit.

- SLA items: SSO/KMS integrations are supported; we need your KMS provider details. There are optional extended-support tiers:
  * Standard (included): 9x5 email + 1-week response for P2; Phone during business hours
  * Premium (+15% platform fee): 24x7 phone + 4-hour P1 response; annual runbook review
  * Enterprise (+30% platform fee): Named TAM, quarterly on-site reviews, 2-hour P1 response

Given Strata's expected data sensitivity and multi-cluster plan, Neha and I recommend offering a three-month migration credit (applies to platform fees only) plus inclusion of 40 engineer-hours for migration tasks. That keeps our commercial concession bounded and gives Strata runway for initial rollout.

I'll attach a short draft SLA with those support tiers.

Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Support: include 40 engineer-hours for migration (applies to KV/cache and tokenizer migration) + Standard support. Option to upgrade to Premium for +15% platform fee.
